title: Total solar eclipse in Spain – level 3
paragraphs: Millions of people across Europe witnessed a spectacular solar eclipse that marked the most significant astronomical event the region has experienced since 1999.

While viewers in Iceland and northern Spain were treated to a total eclipse, onlookers across the United Kingdom experienced a dramatic partial eclipse, with the moon blocking up to 96% of the sun in places like Cornwall. Stargazers gathered in large crowds along coastlines, city monuments, and hills, and wore protective solar glasses to watch the sun transform into a thin crescent. As the peak moment arrived, day turned into darkness, temperatures dropped noticeably, and streetlights turned on, which created an eerie atmosphere for observers.

Scientists and travelers described witnessing the sun’s shimmering corona and nuclear explosions as an unforgettable, humbling experience that reminded them of humanity’s small place in the cosmos. Experts note that a total eclipse will not be visible from the UK again until 2090.
